about.title: About Camiling Water District
about.intro: CWD is a government-owned and controlled corporation (GOCC) chartered under Presidential Decree No. 198, established on December 6, 1976, through Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 132, and became a full-fledged water district on July 27, 1977, with the issuance of Conditional Certificate of Conformance (CCC) No. 43 by the Local Water Utilities Administration (LWUA).
about.mission_body: Camiling Water District exists to provide safe, sufficient, and affordable potable water service to the households, businesses, and institutions of Camiling, Tarlac — delivered with transparency, accountability, and responsiveness to the communities we serve.
about.vision_body: To be a model government water utility in Central Luzon, recognized for dependable service, sound governance, and a modern, responsive relationship with every barangay under our care.
about.leadership_intro: CWD is governed by a Board of Directors and managed day-to-day by the General Manager.
about.partnership_intro: CWD operates in partnership with the private sector to improve service delivery while retaining full public ownership of the water system.
about.jva_heading: Joint Venture with PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation
about.jva_paragraph_1: Camiling Water District (CWD) operates under a Joint Venture Agreement (JVA) with PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation for the financing, development, rehabilitation, upgrading, expansion, operation, and maintenance of the district's potable water supply and septage management systems.
about.jva_paragraph_2: This arrangement falls under the Philippine Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Program. Because water districts cannot, by law, be sold to private corporations, joint venture agreements such as this allow CWD to retain public ownership of the water system while drawing on private-sector capital and technical expertise to improve service delivery to Camiling residents.
about.jva_note_body: PrimeWater Infrastructure Corporation has begun rebranding as Hiraya Water Corporation, following SEC approval in 2025. Both names may appear in official and historical documentation during the transition.
about.service_area_intro: CWD serves 59 of the 61 barangays of the Municipality of Camiling, Tarlac.
about.service_area_note: Barangays Bacsay and Papaac are not currently within the CWD service area, per the district engineer.

careers.title: Careers at CWD
careers.intro: CWD hires in accordance with Civil Service Commission (CSC) rules and merit-based selection. Current openings are posted below as they become available.

application_steps.title: Check requirements
application_steps.description: Each posting lists its own qualification standards (education, experience, training, eligibility).

application_steps.title: Submit application
application_steps.description: Application letter, CSC Personal Data Sheet (Form 212), and supporting documents.

application_steps.title: Initial screening
application_steps.description: HR reviews submissions against the qualification standards for the position.

application_steps.title: Panel interview
application_steps.description: Shortlisted applicants are interviewed by the selection/promotion board.

careers.qualifications_intro: Specific requirements vary by position, but generally follow CSC qualification standards: relevant education, appropriate CSC or professional eligibility, and relevant work experience.

transparency.title: Transparency
transparency.intro: CWD's transparency documents, required under Philippine government web standards.
transparency.seal_paragraph_1: In compliance with Section 93 of the General Appropriations Act and National Budget Circular No. 542, the Camiling Water District (CWD) publishes the following transparency documents on this website.
transparency.seal_paragraph_2: The Transparency Seal is a certificate that CWD has complied with the requirements of Section 93 of the GAA, making government information accessible to every Filipino citizen it serves.
transparency.legal_basis: Basis: RA 11032 (Ease of Doing Business Act) · EO 2 s. 2016 (FOI) · NBC 542 · Section 93, GAA
transparency.charter_intro: CWD's Citizen's Charter describes the step-by-step procedure, requirements, fees, and processing time for each frontline service, as required under the Ease of Doing Business Act (RA 11032).
